draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Guruvayur! This is one of the most important Krishna temples in India, and pilgrims come day and night. More weddings happen here in a day than in most towns in a month.
draft.hungryLine: Guruvayur eats vegetarian. Look for a simple meals hotel near the temple.

moodReplies.show-me-around: See the temple's east gate, then visit Punnathur Kotta, where the temple's elephants live.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the Rudratheertham tank in the evening as the lamps are lit.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The temple has dozens of elephants of its own. A race of them opens the temple festival each year.

legends.title: An elephant who became a legend
legends.body: Guruvayur Kesavan was the temple's most famous elephant. A statue of him stands near the temple.

legends.title: A god brought by a guru
legends.body: The story says Guru, Brihaspati, and Vayu, the wind god, carried the idol here. That's where Guru-vayu-ur gets its name.

tips.title: Darshan queues are shortest early or late.
tips.body: Avoid weekends and auspicious wedding days.

tips.title: Dress code.
tips.body: Men wear a mundu and no shirt inside, women a sari, salwar or long skirt.

story.title: An idol from Dwaraka
story.body: Legend says the idol was rescued from Krishna's city of Dwaraka as it sank into the sea.

story.title: A temple town grows
story.body: Pilgrims came from across Kerala, and the town grew around the temple.

story.title: A fight for entry
story.body: The Guruvayur Satyagraha campaigned for people of all castes to be allowed into the temple.

story.title: Elephants and music
story.body: Punnathur Kotta became the elephants' home, and Chembai music festival brought singers here every year.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Temple at dawn, elephants by day, lamps at the tank by night. Tell me if you saw a wedding.
